summary: Reviewed the canonical web conversion build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s54-twenty-eighth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a.md. Its conversion hash, sha256 c6d57f06ea298bcbb2e305bd1e6c9f5852c092594213774b4e4f2e6d6acc8c85, matches research/web-artifact.json and the REVIEW_INPUTS seal, and regenerating with tools/web-edition from the current sources into scratch reproduced those exact bytes. I compared it with the reviewed research PDF (sha256 9adfbff3..., 38 pages, matching research/artifacts.json) and with the canonical source (main.tex and sections/*.tex). A word-sequence diff of pdftotext output against the rendered page text found no missing or added prose. The only differences were PDF running heads, page numbers and the printed Contents, the reordering of table cells by text extraction, and the H1 title and italic subtitle that the web edition takes from the PDF's pdftitle and pdfsubject, which is the same convention the tracked pc-s51 and pc-s52 editions follow. Several things checked out. The heading hierarchy is one H1, eleven H2s (opening, appointed texts, each element, the three interpretations under their component anchors, comparison, date and location, the two appendices, references) and H3 subsections, with no duplicate ids. The twelve appointed-text anchors proper-* are present. The [TOC] links resolve to all eleven H2s. The three interpretations each end in a definition list of the four senses (Literal, Allegorical, Moral, Anagogical), twelve terms in all. Ten blockquotes render separately, with small-caps source lines and the bracketed italic unappointed verse text set as the PDF sets it. The at-a-glance, comparison and branch tables, and the dossier of nine rows each followed by its own note paragraph, render as tables. There are no backslashes, TeX commands, attribute braces, trailing whitespace or production or model metadata in the Markdown or the rendered text. The revision timestamp and rights colophon are present, and tools/check-web-edition validates the declaration. To judge presentation in a browser, I rendered the page with the site's own renderer (tools/public-alpha render_page and rewrite_links, Python Markdown 3.10.3, the site stylesheet) into scratch, then inspected it in a fresh headless agent-browser session at 1280 px and 390 px. At 1280 px I checked the title block, TOC, quotations, four-senses lists, comparison table, dossier, branch table and closing colophon, and I compared PDF pages 5 and 32 against the corresponding web sections. At 390 px the dossier uses the two-by-two layout the site defines; wide tables scroll inside their container and are not clipped. Limits: I did not fetch the two external USCCB URLs. Italic emphasis was spot-checked visually and not counted exhaustively. The paths of tracked records named in the Scope appendix, and the lane-* component anchors, come from the source and the established converter convention, and the tracked pc-s51 and pc-s52 editions use them identically. Verdict: PASS; no blocking, advisory or accepted findings.
